subject: Script for running stochastic maps over a sample of trees

messages.author: 3614237029e4b209
messages.subject: Script for running stochastic maps over a sample of trees
parts:
Hi everyone,

For a while my research group has been interested in running biogeographic stochastic maps over a sample of trees to account for phylogenetic uncertainty when counting events and estimating the timing of dispersal events. We have finally wrapped up a script that does that, and summarizes the results in a friendly way. It can be found here: https://github.com/ivanlfm/BGB_BSM_multiple_trees

During the elaboration of the script, we found that it is especially useful to include phylogenetic uncertainty when:

(1) one wants to estimate the timing of dispersals using a +J model. This is because in +J models, dispersal is associated to node ages, and using a single tree will mean that the estimate is strongly biased to the age of the node in that particular tree.

(2) one is testing a biogeographic hypothesis and the age estimates cross the boundaries of time slices (as Nick had suggested in an earlier post).

We demonstrate this with a nice example of the colonization of the Galapagos by a group of spiders. If you are interested, you can read the manuscript, which I just posted as a pre-print. It has just been submitted to a journal, so any feedback/comments/suggestions/critiques are mostly welcome:

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.05.11.443682v1

Thanks!
Best,
Ivan
